# root-export-missing-conditions-file

## Requirements

- DeepSeek Harness `>=0.2.0`

# dsh-plugin-toolkit

[![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/dsh-plugin-toolkit)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-plugin-toolkit)
[![downloads](https://img.shields.io/npm/dw/dsh-plugin-toolkit)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-plugin-toolkit)
[![CI](https://github.com/WJDdidi-1/dsh-plugin-toolkit/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/WJDdidi-1/dsh-plugin-toolkit/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![license](https://img.shields.io/npm/l/dsh-plugin-toolkit)](LICENSE)


![dsh-plugin-toolkit](docs/card.png)

English · [中文](./README.zh.md)

Everything a [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) plugin needs between `init` and a version the market index accepts: scaffolding, a test harness for the client bundle, a way to see a change without restarting the app, and a release that does not depend on remembering fourteen steps.

```sh
npx dsh-plugin-toolkit@latest init ./my-panel --name my-panel   # a plugin that already passes the checks
npx dsh-plugin-toolkit@latest verify .                          # pack it, install the tarball, mount the panel
npx dsh-plugin-toolkit@latest release --pr --merge              # tag, wait for npm, update the index, open and merge the PR
```

## The panel

![The Plugin doctor tab, on a plugin that fails two checks](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/WJDdidi-1/dsh-plugin-toolkit/main/docs/panel.png)

The same checks, in the right sidebar: type a folder, an `owner/repo`, or a GitHub link, and it says which one would fail and why. Nothing is installed and nothing is written.

## Three paths

| You are… | Start with | Then |
| --- | --- | --- |
| writing your first plugin | [`init`](#1-write-a-plugin) | `doctor`, `fix`, `verify` |
| changing a panel that is already installed | [`dev`](#2-develop-a-panel) | `mount`, the testkit, `audit` |
| shipping a version | [`verify`](#3-ship-a-version) | `release`, `index` |

It also installs as a plugin. `dsh plugin add dsh-plugin-toolkit` puts a
**插件体检 / Plugin doctor** panel under the conversation and a tab in the right
sidebar. Give it a folder that holds a plugin's `package.json`, or just
`owner/repo` — or a repository name, which it searches GitHub for and lists the
candidates to pick from. It then runs the same checks `verify` runs and says
which one would break the install, with the reason on the line — the same
answers as the CLI, without leaving the app.

```
$ dsh plugin add dsh-plugin-toolkit
```

### 1. Write a plugin

[`init`](#start-from-a-plugin-that-already-passes) writes the files whose absence shows up as a failed first publish — `engines.dsh`, the patch file, a `files` list that ships the code, a client bundle, a test for it, and the CI that runs both. `doctor` then checks the same things without writing anything, and [`verify`](#prove-the-tarball-works-not-just-the-repository) checks the tarball instead of the working copy.

If a plugin already exists, `doctor --fix` turns the failing checks into a
repair plan. It names the file and the edit for every problem, writes nothing
until you add `--write`, and then runs the checks again. `fix --engines` is
still there when the host range is the only thing you need to change.

```sh
npx dsh-plugin-toolkit@latest init ./my-panel --name my-panel
cd my-panel && npm install && npm test && npx dsh-plugin-toolkit@latest doctor .
```

### 2. Develop a panel

A plugin's client code is one file that calls `window.__ModuleLoader__.load({factory})` — there is no module to import, so the usual React test setup does not apply. [`testkit`](#test-a-panel-without-a-browser) supplies the missing half, and [`dev`](#edit-a-plugin-that-is-already-installed) pushes a rebuilt bundle into the running app.

```sh
npx dsh-plugin-toolkit@latest mount ./client.js     # what a user would see, without the app
npx dsh-plugin-toolkit@latest dev . --host http://127.0.0.1:54133
```

### 3. Ship a version

`verify` first (it is the only check that reads the tarball), then `release`, which tags, waits for the registry, writes the index entry with the publish time the registry reports, and — with `--pr --merge` — opens and merges the pull request.

```sh
npx dsh-plugin-toolkit@latest verify .
npx dsh-plugin-toolkit@latest release . --pr --merge
```

## What `verify` actually does

![Five steps, and the failure each one catches](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/WJDdidi-1/dsh-plugin-toolkit/main/docs/pipeline.svg)

The order matters. Packing first means the check reads the file list npm will publish, not the folder you have. Installing the tarball means the root is imported by its bare specifier — the package name the loader uses — not by a file path taken from `main` or `exports["."]`. Node ignores `main` once `exports` exists, so a package whose `exports` map has no `"."` entry fails with `ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED` at that step even though the file is present. Mounting means the client bundle is actually executed, in jsdom, with a host that records what it registered.

Each step exists because a plugin once got past the step before it and still installed into nothing.

## Why this exists

Releasing one plugin fifteen times taught me three things the ecosystem's tooling does not cover:

1. **A version is not shipped when npm accepts it.** Registry propagation took two to eight minutes every time. `npm view` answered from a stale local cache, so I repeatedly believed a release had failed when it had not — and once believed it had succeeded when the market still could not see it.
2. **The market index is a second release, done by hand.** Each version needs an entry carrying `publishTimestamp` from the registry and `engines.dsh` from the manifest. Forget the range and the index validator rejects the PR with `Engines mismatch` — after the tag is already public.
3. **Reading a manifest is not the same as checking it.** A plugin can have a valid `package.json` and still be uninstallable: `files` that omit the entry the manifest points at, a bundle patch that does not exist, a README that never states the host range it declares.

The five failures behind these checks — a red dot with no panel, a row the host drops, an app that disables every plugin after one unguarded `apply()`, a tab nothing can open, and a checker that was wrong — are written up with their exact error text and how to reproduce each one: [Five plugins that installed and did nothing](https://github.com/WJDdidi-1/dsh-plugin-toolkit/blob/main/docs/why-it-exists.md).

### Four ways a plugin installs and still does nothing

Each of these shipped in a real version of this toolkit before the check below existed. A manifest check passes on all four.

| What you see | What it was | Caught by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The tab is a red dot and the panel never opens | `exports["."]` pointed at the CLI, so the loader's row had no plugin to apply | `root export` |
| The plugin is installed, the app never serves it | `dsh.client` declared, `exports["./client"]` missing — the host drops the row | `client declaration` |
| The app says the third-party plugin is unsupported and disables all of them | `apply()` read `ctx.webServer` without declaring it; cordis throws instead of returning `undefined` | `verify` (calls `apply` on a context that has no services) |
| The tab registers, and nothing in the UI opens it | `sidebarRightTabs.register()` registers a *type*; the sidebar lists what `tabs.guide()` returns | a testkit test, not `doctor` |

The first three are static: `doctor` and `verify` catch them without the app running. The fourth is a UI contract, so it needs the panel mounted and the registration inspected — that is what [`testkit`](#test-a-panel-without-a-browser) is for.

## Requirements

- Node.js 18 or newer (the registry is read with `fetch`; no runtime dependencies)
- Git and `gh` on `PATH` for the steps that touch GitHub
- DeepSeek Harness `>=0.2.0` — the version whose market index carries `engines.dsh`, which is what makes the range check meaningful
- For `testkit`: `jsdom`, `react` and `react-dom` as dev dependencies (`npm install --save-dev jsdom react react-dom`)

## Start from a plugin that already passes

```sh
$ npx dsh-plugin-toolkit@latest init ./my-panel --name my-panel --title "My panel"
created 8 file(s) in /Users/you/my-panel
  .github/workflows/ci.yml
  .gitignore
  README.md
  client.js
  cordis.patch.yml
  index.js
  package.json
  test/panel.test.mjs

next: npm install && npm test && npm run doctor
```

What you get is not a snippet: it is a plugin whose `doctor` already passes (`engines.dsh`, the patch file, the `files` list), with a client bundle that registers a sidebar tab, a testkit test for it, and a CI workflow that runs both. `init` refuses a directory that is not empty unless you pass `--force`, and refuses a name npm would refuse — those are the two mistakes that cost the most time later.

Every command that takes a path expands a leading `~` before touching the filesystem. The tool, not the shell, expands `~` for these arguments: `cmd` and PowerShell pass `"~/my-panel"` through literally, while a POSIX shell usually expands it first. `init '~/my-panel' --name my-panel` writes into your home directory (the same files `init ~/my-panel` writes on a POSIX shell), and `doctor '~/my-panel'` reads it back. The Windows spelling `~\my-panel` works too; a directory literally named `~` is never created.

## Where it lives

The checker is docked **under the conversation**, above the input bar: a single
row, collapsed by default. Open it and it carries the whole guide — who it is
for, how to use it, what each check means, and what it cannot tell you — plus
the folder field and the results. The same panel is also a **Plugin doctor** tab
in the right sidebar, for when the conversation is busy.

The panel speaks both languages and opens in Chinese; the 中文 / EN switch sits
in the dock's header row (and in the sidebar tab) and the choice is remembered.

Look at it without the app. The preview mounts the panel with the testkit, so it
needs the optional peers; install them once with
`npm install --save-dev jsdom react react-dom`:

```sh
node scripts/preview.mjs /tmp/panel.html   # collapsed, open, with a result, and the tab
```

## Test a panel without a browser

A plugin's client code is one file that calls `window.__ModuleLoader__.load({factory})` — there is no module to import, so the usual React test setup does not apply. `testkit` supplies the missing half: a DOM, the real React, and a host context that records what the panel registers.

```sh
npm install --save-dev jsdom react react-dom
```

```js
import { mountClient, createFetch } from 'dsh-plugin-toolkit/testkit';

const panel = await mountClient({
  file: 'client.js',
  copy: { 'my-plugin': { title: 'My panel' } },
  fetch: createFetch({
    '/my-plugin/report': { body: { score: 71, noise: 3 } },
    '/my-plugin/apply': () => ({ status: 201, body: { score: 92 } }),
  }),
});

await panel.click('[data-testid="optimize"]');
console.assert(panel.text().includes('92'), 'the score on screen did not move');
console.assert(panel.must('[role="status"]').textContent.includes('92'));
await panel.unmount();
```

`unmount()` is async: it lets React finish the work its own unmount schedules before the DOM goes away. Skipping the `await` surfaces as `ReferenceError: window is not defined` *after* the test has already passed, which is a confusing way to learn it.

What you get back: `text()`, `html()`, `query(selector)`, `must(selector)` (throws with the rendered HTML when it misses), `click(selector)`, `type(selector, value)`, `press(selector, key)`, `focus`, `attributes(selector)`, `snapshot(dir, name)` for a normalised DOM baseline, and `host` for assertions about what the bundle registered.

### Keep a visual baseline

The DOM is the baseline: normalising class order and whitespace gives a file that fails for the reasons a screenshot would — a lost label, a control that stopped rendering — and can be reviewed in a diff instead of by eye.

```js
import { expectSnapshot } from 'dsh-plugin-toolkit/testkit';

const panel = await mountClient({ file: 'client.js' });
expectSnapshot(panel.html(), '__snapshots__', 'panel');   // throws with the element that moved
await panel.unmount();
```

First run writes nothing: it tells you to re-run with `UPDATE_SNAPSHOTS=1`, so a baseline is always a decision, never a side effect. That rerun writes the normalised HTML and returns `{ status: 'written' }`; later runs return `same` or fail with the element that moved.

### Check what assistive tech sees

```js
panel.expectAria('[role="tab"][aria-selected="true"]', { label: 'Protection', selected: 'true' });
assert.match(panel.must('[role="status"]').textContent, /Score moved 71 → 77/);
```

`expectAria()` compares the attributes a screen reader actually reads — `role`,
`label`, `live`, `selected`, `expanded`, `checked`, `pressed`, `disabled` — and
names the one that differs:

```
[aria-live="polite"]: expected aria text to be "9", but it is "0"
```

A missing attribute is reported as `nothing`, not as an empty string, because
those are different bugs. `panel.aria(selector)` returns the same object when you
want to assert on it yourself.

`must()` throws with the rendered markup when the selector misses, which is the difference between "the assertion failed" and "here is what the user actually got".

Every example below is shipped in the package, run by CI, and the output shown is the output it prints:

| Example | What it shows |
| --- | --- |
| `node examples/mount-a-bundle.mjs` | mount a real bundle, read the text, click, read it again |
| `node examples/route-stubs.mjs` | answer the routes a panel asks for, and assert on the requests |
| `node examples/baseline.mjs` | a DOM baseline compared on every run |
| `node examples/aria.mjs` | what assistive tech sees |

```sh
$ node examples/mount-a-bundle.mjs
Demo panel Count 0 0
Demo panel Count 1 1
```

```sh
$ node examples/route-stubs.mjs
Score 71
asked for: 1 route(s), undeclared route answers 404
```

To look at a bundle by hand:

```sh
npx dsh-plugin mount ./client.js            # print the text a user would see
npx dsh-plugin mount ./client.js --html     # print the markup
```

That is how the AIignore panel was checked before release: the real bundle, mounted in Node, against a stubbed `/aiignore/*`:

```
$ npx dsh-plugin mount ../ai-context-doctor/plugin/client.js
AIignore No workspace yet Could not read the report …
```

## Put the badge on a plugin that passes

If `verify` passes on your plugin, this badge says so and links back here:

```md
[![checked with dsh-plugin-toolkit](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/WJDdidi-1/dsh-plugin-toolkit/main/docs/badge.svg)](https://github.com/WJDdidi-1/dsh-plugin-toolkit)
```

It is a claim, not a decoration: add it only when `dsh-plugin verify .` exits 0.

## Start from the example

[`dsh-plugin-example`](https://github.com/WJDdidi-1/dsh-plugin-example) is a ~70-line plugin: one sidebar tab, two languages, one behaviour test, CI that runs `verify` through the composite action. It is the shape this toolkit expects, so it is also the fastest way to see whether the toolkit fits your plugin. It is a GitHub template too: **Use this template** starts you on a plugin whose first publish already passes.

```sh
dsh plugin add dsh-plugin-example
```

## See what is installed, and what the app loaded

`doctor` checks one folder you name. The question that actually gets asked is
"why is my plugin not in the sidebar?", and the answer needs three things at once:
what is installed, whether each installed copy is valid, and which of them the
running app actually loaded.

```sh
$ dsh-plugin audit --host http://127.0.0.1:54133
dsh-aiignore           0.37.1    loaded       ok
demo-panel             0.3.0     not loaded   ok  — dsh.profile.bundles in /Users/me/.dsh/profiles/desktop/package.json does not list it, and the loader mounts only listed bundles
                                            fix: add "demo-panel" to dsh.profile.bundles in /Users/me/.dsh/profiles/desktop/package.json (or run `dsh plugin add demo-panel`), then restart the app

1 installed plugin(s) are not in the running app:
```

"Not loaded" has three different causes, and `audit` names the one that applies
instead of offering a blanket restart:

- **Not in `dsh.profile.bundles`.** `pnpm add` (or `npm install`) installs the
  package but does not tell the loader to mount it. Add the package name to
  `dsh.profile.bundles` in `~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/package.json`, or run
  `dsh plugin add <name>`, then restart the app.
- **No `dsh.bundle`.** The package declares `dsh` but no patch file to mount.
  Add `dsh.bundle.patch` to its `package.json` and ship the patch file, then
  reinstall.
- **Listed, but the app predates the install.** The profile is already correct;
  restart the app once to read the new list.

Advisories (`engines.dsh`, README Requirements) are counted apart from problems:
the market index needs them, the loader does not, so they should not bury a plugin
that is actually broken.

`audit` exits `1` when an installed plugin has a hard failure **or** when the
running app did not load at least one installed plugin, so CI can gate on a
profile where the app silently skipped a plugin. It exits `0` when every
installed plugin is loaded and valid. When `--host` is given but the app cannot
be reached, the command has not observed the graph it was asked for: it prints
the `/plugins/events` URL it could not read, prints no plugin rows or clean
summary, and exits `2` so a CI gate cannot pass against an unreachable app.
Without `--host`, the loaded column is `?` and only hard failures change the
exit code.

`audit --home <dir>` scans a different profile home; both `~/.dsh` and
`~\.dsh` expand. A bare `--home`, or one followed by another flag such as
`--timeout 50` or `--json`, is a missing value rather than a request to scan
`$HOME/.dsh` or a folder literally named after the flag: the command exits `2`,
names `--home`, and prints no profile report.

Without `--host` the loaded column is `?`, because guessing would be worse than
saying nothing. Only packages that declare a `dsh` field are audited — the rest of
`node_modules` is ordinary dependencies, and auditing those is noise.

An installed package whose `package.json` cannot be read is the exception: the
`dsh` field that would mark it as a plugin is in the file that failed to parse.
If its name is still in `dsh.profile.bundles`, `audit` reports a `manifest`
failure naming the unreadable `package.json` and exits `1` instead of treating
the folder as an ordinary dependency. A truncated manifest from an interrupted
install therefore cannot make the plugin disappear from the report, and a valid
sibling plugin is still listed on the same run. The exception stays narrow: a
damaged `package.json` in a package that is neither in `dsh.profile.bundles` nor
readable enough to expose a `dsh` field is still an ordinary dependency and is
skipped, so one broken transitive install does not fail every audit.

A declared bundle can also be missing entirely. If a name stays in
`dsh.profile.bundles` after its `node_modules/<name>` folder is removed (an
interrupted install, or a package deleted by hand), `audit` prints a `missing`
row with an `install` failure naming the absent folder and exits `1`, while
still listing the healthy plugins on the same run. An absent package that the
profile never declared is not an install record, so it is not invented in the
report; a regression test removes the name from the profile and requires the
shipped CLI to exit `0` without printing it.

## Edit a plugin that is already installed

The host already swaps a rebuilt bundle without a page reload: it watches each plugin's entry artifact and reports a `rebuilt` frame on `/plugins/events`. `dev` puts the new file where the host is looking, then **proves** the frame arrived instead of asking you to check by eye.

```sh
npx dsh-plugin dev . --host http://127.0.0.1:54133
```

![dsh-plugin dev printing the revision the app reported](docs/dev.gif)

*Recorded from a real run against the running app: the last line is the revision the app sent back on `/plugins/events`, not a message the tool printed on faith.*

```
demo-aiignore: /work/plugin/client.js -> ~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/node_modules/dsh-aiignore/client.js
initial: copied 163647 bytes at 1:18:43 AM
reloaded dsh-aiignore (rev e0c0230c4fc9)
watching /work/plugin
```

That last line is the whole point: the revision came back from the app's own event stream, so "it reloaded" is a fact, not a hope.

A plugin the running app never loaded cannot be reloaded, and the app says so by leaving it out of the graph it sends first. `dev` reads that graph, so a freshly installed plugin gets the sentence that fixes it instead of a timeout:

```
copied, but not confirmed: the running app has not loaded demo-panel, so it will not report a reload; restart the app once after installing it
```

| Flag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--dest <dir>` | write into this installed copy instead of searching `~/.dsh/profiles/*/node_modules/<name>` |
| `--entry <file>` | copy this file instead of `dsh.client.entry`, `client.js`, `lib/client.js` |
| `--build <command>` | run this before each copy (a failed build copies nothing) |
| `--host <url>` | confirm the reload against the app at this URL; without it the copy still happens and the tool says it is unconfirmed |
| `--once` | copy once and exit, for scripts |

Two things it does not do, because the host does not: React state inside the reloaded plugin is lost, and a failed swap does not roll back to the previous bundle.

## Use it in CI

The same checks run as a GitHub Action, so a tag cannot go out on a plugin that would not install:

```yaml
- uses: actions/checkout@v4
- uses: WJDdidi-1/dsh-plugin-toolkit@v1
  with:
    dir: plugin        # the folder holding the plugin's package.json
    command: verify    # pack it, install the tarball, mount the panel
```

`verify` is the default because it is the only check that reads what a user
actually installs: `doctor` reads the working copy, so a `files` list that
forgets `client.js` passes it and fails only after `npm i`.

`command: doctor` stops at the manifest checks (fast, no install), and
`command: index` audits `market/index.json` instead, failing on any version whose
`engines.dsh` is missing or is not a semver range (a malformed value such as
`>=banana`, or a single pinned version such as `0.2.0`, both fail). Pin
`version:` if you would rather not track the latest release.

## Check a plugin you have not cloned

The panel takes three kinds of input: a folder, `owner/repo`, or a GitHub URL.
A bare name is a search, not a guess — it asks GitHub, lists the matches with
their stars, and checks the one you pick. A repository is downloaded once as a
tarball into a temp folder, so nothing is cloned into your workspace and
nothing is installed.

The CLI reads a repository straight from the GitHub API:

```bash
dsh-plugin doctor --remote V1ki/dsh-plugin-subscriptions
```

```text
dsh-plugin doctor: 1 problem(s) in V1ki/dsh-plugin-subscriptions
  ⨯ engines.dsh: engines.dsh is missing, so a host that enforces the range rejects the install as "incompatible with dsh"; declare the range you support, e.g. "engines": { "dsh": ">=0.2.0" }
```

That is the whole reason this mode exists: the plugin hub files failed installs
back into plugin repositories, and the report is a sentence — `plugin install
failed`, `plugin does not support the DSH version in use` — that never names a
file. Reading `package.json` over the API is enough to name it.

What it can see, and what it cannot:

- Manifest checks (`engines.dsh`, `dsh field`, `files`, `dsh.client`,
  `exports`) run on the real `package.json`.
- README checks (`readme`) run on the text GitHub serves: the README must have
  a `Requirements` heading and must state the host range `package.json`
  declares. A repository whose checkout fails `readme` fails the remote check
  too, with the same sentence.
- File checks (does `exports["./client"]` point at a file that exists, does the
  root export `apply`) need the tree. npm runs `prepack` and `prepare` before
  `npm pack` creates the tarball, and `prepublishOnly` before `npm publish`
  does, so a package whose lifecycle hook builds those files publishes files it
  does not commit: those checks are **skipped with a note** instead of calling a
  working plugin broken. A plain `build` script is not a lifecycle hook and is
  not evidence by itself, because npm never runs it unless `prepack` or
  `prepare` calls it; put the build there if it produces shipped files.
- Public repositories work anonymously, but GitHub allows 60 requests an hour.
  Export `GH_TOKEN` (or `GITHUB_TOKEN`) to audit more than one or two.

To check a whole list in one pass, put one `owner/repo` per line in a file and
pass it with `--from` (`-` reads standard input):

```sh
$ dsh-plugin audit --remote --from repos.txt
```

Repositories are read four at a time by default. `--jobs N` changes that width;
values above `8` are capped at `8`, and `--jobs 1` walks the list one repository
at a time, the timing the command had before batching. The output — and the
`--json` array — still follows the input list, and every verdict is the one the
sequential run produced, so a diff between two runs compares repositories rather
than scheduling.

When GitHub answers `403` or `429`, the shared quota is gone, so the batch stops
starting new repositories and marks every entry it could not read as
`rate-limited` instead of `clean` or `unreadable`. If the response carries
`x-ratelimit-reset` (or `retry-after`), the reset time is printed with the
verdict, and the remaining entries are reported without another request.

### Will this plugin install on my DSH?

The fifteen compatibility reports, from four repositories, all end with the same
question. Add `--host <version>` to a remote audit and it answers that question
for one repository. This is the output for `L3n3L/dsh-resume`, a real plugin
whose declared range stops before DSH 0.2.0, checked against the
`0.2.2-alpha.3` canary from the reports. The checked-in sample is a frozen 0.1.3
snapshot, so the line stays true as the upstream repository changes:

```sh
$ dsh-plugin audit --remote L3n3L/dsh-resume --host 0.2.2-alpha.3
incompatible  L3n3L/dsh-resume  0.1.3 (host >=0.1.0-rc.6 <0.2.0-0) [incompatible with dsh 0.2.2-alpha.3; declares ">=0.1.0-rc.6 <0.2.0-0"]

summary: 1 repository — 0 clean, 1 failing (1 problem), 0 unreadable, 0 rate-limited
```

The verdict comes first: `incompatible` means the range in `package.json` does
not accept the host, so the installer rejects the plugin before it unpacks it.
This run exits `1`. The same answer is reproducible without a GitHub request:
the checked-in snapshot under `examples/compatibility-sample/` keeps the 0.1.3
manifest fields that decide compatibility, and its `## Requirements` heading
isolates the host-range answer. This command feeds that snapshot through the
real CLI path:

```sh
$ node scripts/compatibility-sample.mjs
```

(`npm run compatibility` runs the same script.) The script starts the shipped
`bin/dsh-plugin.mjs` as a child process and answers its GitHub reads from the
checked-in folder, so the block above is that executable's stdout rather than a
library shortcut; it exits `0` only after the replayed command exited `1`. The
test suite runs the script and compares its output with the block above, so the
sample cannot drift from the flag parser, the formatter, or the README. Running
`dsh-plugin audit --remote L3n3L/dsh-resume --host 0.2.2-alpha.3` without the
sample audits the repository's current default branch instead; a README or
manifest change since 0.1.3 can add another `readme` or manifest failure to the
same row.

CI should read the same answer as data. This is the reproducible sample again,
with the flag that changes the form rather than the verdict:

```sh
$ node scripts/compatibility-sample.mjs --json
[
  {
    "target": "L3n3L/dsh-resume",
    "version": "0.1.3",
    "hostRange": ">=0.1.0-rc.6 <0.2.0-0",
    "failures": [],
    "notes": [],
    "host": "0.2.2-alpha.3",
    "compatibility": "incompatible"
  }
]
```

`compatibility` is the finding for an incompatible range; the object does not
invent a second entry in `failures` for the same fact. Gate on `compatibility`
or the process exit code, not on `failures.length` alone, or a host mismatch
will look clean. The command still exits `1`, and the test suite compares this
block with the JSON the executable prints, so the documented shape cannot drift
from the code that emits it.

The line carries the range `package.json` declares and one of `compatible`,
`incompatible`, or `unknown` against that host version. `unknown` is the honest
answer for a missing or malformed range — there is nothing to compare — while a
range that excludes the host is `incompatible`, counted as failing, and exits
`1`. npm's pre-release rule is part of the answer: `>=0.2.0` does not accept
`0.2.2-alpha.3`, because a range only opts into a pre-release when it names one
of the same `major.minor.patch`. A canary host can therefore be `incompatible`
with a range that will accept the final release. The same flag works in the
batch mode, so one `--from` run answers the whole list:

```sh
$ dsh-plugin audit --remote --from repos.txt --host 0.2.2-alpha.3
```

The compatibility flags are `--remote <owner/repo>` for one repository,
`--from <file>` for a list (`-` reads standard input), `--host <version>` for
the DSH version to compare against, and `--json` for the machine-readable
finding. `--jobs <n>` sets the batch width, and `--patch-dir <dir>` writes the
host-targeted repair for each repository that needs one. The help text lists
the same flags; a test fails if this section n

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# dsh-workbench · 墨鱼创作工作台 **当前版本：`0.2.4`** DeepSeek Harness（DSH）桌面端插件。把公众号内容生产的完整链路收进一个面板： **找选题 → 写稿 → 审稿 → 配图 → 排版 → 发到草稿箱**。 它不是一堆对话式工具，而是一个**面板产品**——左侧栏多出菜单项，进去是标签页， 数据落在工作区的 SQLite 里，Agent 与界面共用同一份。 --- ## 一、这是什么 | 项目 | 说明 | |---|---| | 版本 | `0.2.4` | | 形态 | DSH 插件（bundle patch + web client 半 + node 半） | | 面向 | 公众号运营、自媒体作者、内容团队 | | 核心 | 三个子工作台：**公众号**、**绘图**、**技能库**，侧边栏一个入口进入，顶部切换条切换 | | 数据 | 工作区内的 SQLite（`/workbench/workbench.db`，10 张业务表） | | 联网 | 装完即用；抓素材、配图等需联网的环节按需触发 | --- ## 二、功能 ### 2.1 三个工作台 侧边栏只有一个入口「墨鱼创作工作台」。进去后顶部是一排切换标签： **公众号 / 绘图 / 技能库 / 设置**。前三个是子工作台，设置是全局配置页。 **公众号**（8 个模块） | 模块 | 做什么 | |---|---| | 每日热榜 | 7 路来源的当日热榜，支持 7 天归档回溯 | | 爆文库 | 公众号 22 个分类 + 小红书 25 个分类的存量爆款，带封面与互动数 | | 选题库 | 一行一个选题方案，可按赛道筛选、一键去创作 | | 创作台 | 左配置右预览的写稿台，选题预设带进来，边写边看进度 | | 我的创作 | 草稿全生命周期管理，8 个阶段从待写到已群发 | | 发布管理 | 发布动作记录，草稿箱与群发分开记账 | | 风格库 | 文字风格（语气变体）的量化定义与自检 | | 技能包 | 该工作台用到哪些技能、挂在哪个阶段 | #### 每日热榜 共 7 路来源：今日头条 / 百度 / 抖音 直取官方榜单，微博 / 知乎 走聚合接口， AI·热点 / AI·资讯 走 AIHOT。保留最近 7 天可回溯，每路可展开看完整榜单， 逐条点【生成选题】进入选题流程，已生成的可【再生成】。 ![每日热榜](./assets/shot-hotlist.png) #### 爆文库 每日 18:30 同步前一天的 10w+ 榜单，覆盖公众号 22 个分类，带封面、阅读数、 在看/赞/转数据，可一键【生成选题】或【打开原文】。 分「公众号爆文 / 小红书爆文 / 采集爆文」三栏，可按日期、分类、热度或关键词筛选。 ![爆文库](./assets/shot-viral.png) #### 选题库 一行一个选题方案（一个方案 = 一个角度，不是一个标题）。每张卡片给出作者观点、 写作切入角度、读者为什么点，以及**发布前核验**提示（缺哪些素材）， 可按赛道、来源筛选，确认后点【去创作】进入创作台。 ![选题库](./assets/shot-topics.png) #### 创作台 左边选写作技能（公众号写稿 / 娱乐成稿 / 卡兹克长文）与创作风格，填主题和核心角度， 右边实时看生成进度，写完直接出全文。选题带进来的预设会自动回填，不用重新描述一遍。 风格是一份完整的写作提示词，选中后会把全文送进写作指令；不选则按技能默认。 ![创作台](./assets/shot-create.png) #### 我的创作 共 8 个阶段：待写 → 初稿 → 已打磨 → 已审稿 → 已排版 → 已配图 → 已入草稿箱 → 已群发。 每条显示封面、来源选题、赛道、写作技能、字数与进度条，可从任意阶段【编辑】或【详情】， 再推进到【入草稿箱】。 ![我的创作](./assets/shot-mine.png) **绘图**（7 个模块） | 模块 | 做什么 | |---|---| | 漫图创作 | 左表单右预览，选风格/图型/色卡后组提示词出图 | | 风格库 | 手绘风格库，含编号参考图 | | 图型库 | 排版图型库 | | 主色调 | 经典单色色卡 | | 角色资产库 | 角色 / 道具 / 场景三类资产，可复用到后续创作 | | 我的创作 | 生成结果归档，按张计费 | | 技能包 | 该工作台用到哪些技能 | **技能库** 集中查看随包分发的 50 个技能，按工作台分组，显示每个技能的用途、脚本与路径。 **设置** 全局配置页，是切换条上的第四个标签，不属于任何一个子工作台。分四组， 每组标题右边有作用范围标签： | 分组 | 用在哪 | |---|---| | 生图 | **共用·出图**：公众号的「配图」和绘图出图都读这一组 | | 文本模型 | **仅绘图台·文字功能**：主题润色与 AI 智能分镜用 | | 公众号 | 微信 AppID / AppSecret、Redfox Key、账号槽位 | | 行为 | 骨架确认开关、热榜保留天数 | #### 风格库 367 种手绘与实拍风格，按 FA–FI 九组分类： | 组 | 数量 | 风格方向 | |---|---|---| | FA | 40 | 国际社论幽默 | | FB | 66 | 经典绘本叙事 | | FC | 32 | 现代平面艺术 | | FD | 42 | 日本当代插画 | | FE | 68 | 新国风与传统工艺 | | FF | 17 | 3D 黏土毛毡与纸雕 | | FG | 24 | 动漫和赛璐璐 | | FH | 44 | 先锋实验与综合媒介 | | FI | 34 | 写实摄影与视觉大片 | 卡片上是组内编号与中英名称（如 `FE-059`），可按编号、作者、关键词搜索； 也可以自建风格，自建的会归到 CS 组，只存在本地、不进随包数据。 ![风格库](./assets/shot-style.png) ### 2.2 创作流水线 ``` 每日热榜 / 爆文库 │ 点【生成选题】→ 填预设 → 入队 ▼ 待分析队列 ──▶ Agent 跑选题技能 │ ▼ 选题库（一行 = 一个方案）── 点【去创作】 │ ▼ 创作台 ──▶ 我的创作：排队 → 草稿 → 打磨 → 审稿 → 排版 → 配图 → 入草稿箱 → 群发 │ │ │ │ │ │ ▼ ▼ ▼ ▼ ▼ ▼ draft.md review.md article.md article.html imgs/*.png publishes 记录 ``` 每个阶段都有对应的检查脚本，产物不合格会被拦下。 **连续创作还是逐段确认**，由设置页「骨架要人工确认」决定： | 开关 | 行为 | |---|---| | 不勾（默认） | **一次做完**：从当前阶段一路推到「已排版」（图位插好）才停，中间回写状态不停下问 | | 勾上 | 逐段汇报：第②③④步产物先给你看，骨架后等你确认再写正文 | 两种模式下，配图和发布都由你手工发起，自动流程的终点是「图位插好」。 ### 2.3 素材来源 | 平台 | 来源 | |---|---| | 今日头条 / 百度 / 抖音 | 各自官方榜单接口 | | 微博 / 知乎 | 60s 聚合接口 | | AI·热点 / AI·资讯 | AIHOT 接口（多源交叉，带摘要） | 以上 5 个平台 + AIHOT 两个分类，合计 7 路来源。某一路当天抓取失败时会缺席， 所以页面上的「共 N 路」按当天实际抓到的数量显示。 也支持**手动投料**：每日热榜 →「手动投料」→ 贴文字 + 传图片（单张 ≤12MB）。 ### 2.4 赛道 8 类，用于决定选题方向与写作技能： 社会民生 · 娱乐与情感 · AI 与科技 · 国际与时事 · 财经与商业 · 文化与生活 · 体育与健康 · 教育与职场 另有「自动判断」选项，由 Agent 按标题决定。 --- ## 三、架构 ### 3.1 三层结构 | 层 | 文件 | 职责 | |---|---|---| | client 半 | `lib/client.template.js` → 生成 `lib/client.js` | 界面：标签页、弹窗、抽屉、全文阅读。注册 `main` + `sidebar.panellist` 槽位 | | node 半 | `lib/index.js` | 带鉴权的 HTTP 路由（21 条，全部挂在 `/api/workbench/` 下）。界面与磁盘之间的桥 | | 数据层 | `tools/workbench-db.py` / `tools/image-db.py` | SQLite 访问，Agent 直接调，node 半通过 `execFile` 调 | SQLite 访问绕一层 Python，是因为给 Electron 编译 `better-sqlite3` 存在 ABI 问题， 而 Python 标准库 `sqlite3` 零依赖。 > 改界面请改 `lib/client.template.js`，再跑 `tools/build.py` 生成 `lib/client.js`。 > 直接改 `client.js` 会在下次生成时被覆盖。 ### 3.2 数据层 库文件：`/workbench/workbench.db`，共 10 张业务表。 | 表 | 作用 | |---|---| | `topic_jobs` | 待分析队列 | | `topics` | 选题库（一行 = 一个选题方案） | | `drafts` | 我的创作（一行 = 一篇稿） | | `publishes` | 发布动作记录 | | `writing_styles` | 文字风格库（一行 = 一种语气） | | `settings` | 设置项（密钥 / 行为开关，一行一个 key） | | `image_jobs` | 生图任务队列 | | `image_assets` | 生成物（一行 = 一张图） | | `image_usage` | 生图计费账本 | | `image_series` | 漫画流（一次创作 = 一组分镜） | **状态机** ``` topic_jobs : pending → running → done / failed topics : candidate → selected → writing → done / dropped drafts : queued → draft → polished → reviewed → formatted → illustrated → draftbox → published image_jobs : queued → running → done / failed image_series: draft → queued → running → done / failed ``` `drafts.status` 管**内容进度**，`publishes` 管**发布动作**，两个轴分开记。 `draftbox`（已入草稿箱）与 `published`（已群发）必须区分，否则界面会显示错误状态。 **创作配置字段** `drafts` 表含四个创作配置列： | 列 | 内容 | |---|---| | `theme` | 创作主题（用户输入原文） | | `materials` | 参考素材（粘贴正文，≤5000 字） | | `requirement` | 用户要求（观点 / 风格 / 角度） | | `config_json` | 结构化配置：`{words, wordKey, styleTab, styleKey}` | ### 3.3 目录结构 ``` dsh-workbench/ ├── package.json dsh.bundle.patch + dsh.client.platform:web ├── cordis.patch.yml 插件挂载声明 ├── install.py 一键安装 ├── lib/ │ ├── index.js node 半：21 条路由 + mdToHtml 转换器 │ ├── client.template.js client 半源码（改这个） │ └── client.js 生成物（不要手改） ├── tools/ 命令行工具（建库、检查、抓数、生图、构建） ├── skills/ 50 个依赖技能（技能库） ├── writing-dna/ 写作风格分析方法论 ├── skills-manifest.json 技能清单（机器可读） ├── SKILLS-CREDITS.md 技能来源与许可证 └── README.md ``` --- ## 四、安装 ### 4.1 环境要求 | 项 | 要求 | |---|---| | 系统 | Windows / macOS / Linux | | Python | 3.9 或更高（安装器会自检） | | DSH | 桌面端已安装并至少启动过一次 | | 磁盘 | 约 120 MB（含技能库） | | 网络 | 安装阶段不需要；使用抓数、配图功能时需要 | ### 4.2 安装步骤 ```bash python install.py # 自动完成全部步骤 python install.py --check # 只检查环境，不做任何改动 python install.py --no-net # 跳过上游补下载（技能随包分发，通常用不到） ``` 安装器会依次完成： 1. 检查 Python 版本与必需目录 2. 初始化数据库（10 张业务表）并预置设置项 3. 安装依赖技能到 `$DSH_HOME/skills/` 4. 生成 `lib/client.js`（界面代码） 5. 检查插件挂载情况，给出下一步指令 6. 生成安装报告 技能必须排在生成界面代码**之前**：技能库快照是从磁盘扫描 `$DSH_HOME/skills/` 得到的， 先装技能再生成，技能库才不会是空的。 技能随包分发，**安装阶段不需要联网**。若包内缺某个技能（手工删过或使用精简包）， 会自动按 `skills-manifest.json` 从上游补下载；断网也不影响安装完成，只是对应功能会提示缺技能。 ### 4.3 挂载到 DSH 安装器会打印当前状态。若尚未挂载，需要改 profile 的 `package.json` 并建立链接。 **先做这一步，两种情况都要**：**完全退出 DSH**（关窗口不够，托盘也要退， 确认任务管理器里没有 DSH 进程）。client 半按模块 id 加载，必须重启进程才生效； 而且 DSH 运行时**会占用 profile 目录**，不停掉会导致下一步写文件失败。 profile 位置：`%USERPROFILE%\.dsh\profiles\desktop\` 改 `package.json`，两处： ```json { "dependencies": { "dsh-workbench": "link:C:/path/to/dsh-workbench" }, "dsh": { "profile": { "bundles": ["dsh-workbench"] } } } ``` > 路径用正斜杠 `/`，或写成转义后的双反斜杠 `\\`。`bundles` 是往已有数组里**追加**， > 别把原有项覆盖掉。 然后用下面任一方式建立链接。 #### 方式 A：pnpm install（常规） 在 profile 目录执行： ```bash pnpm install ``` #### 方式 B：手工建软链（免 pnpm，推荐作为备选） 本插件**零运行时依赖**（`package.json` 没有 `dependencies`，四个 peer 全部 optional）， `pnpm install` 在这里只干一件事：把插件目录链到 `node_modules`。这一步手工也能做： **Windows**（目录联接 junction，**不需要管理员权限**）： ```powershell cmd /c mklink /J "%USERPROFILE%\.dsh\profiles\desktop\node_modules\dsh-workbench" "C:\path\to\dsh-workbench" ``` **macOS / Linux**（符号链接）： ```bash mkdir -p ~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/node_modules ln -sfn "/path/to/dsh-workbench" ~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/node_modules/dsh-workbench ``` 若提示已存在，先删掉旧的再建。 做完启动 DSH，左侧栏会出现「墨鱼创作工作台」入口，点进去即用。 #### 如果 pnpm 报 EPERM（Windows） ``` [EPERM] rename '...\package.json.358186889' -> '...\package.json' ``` 这不是权限坏了，是 **`package.json` 被占用**。pnpm 改文件的方式是「写临时文件 → rename 覆盖」， rename 要求目标文件没有任何进程持有句柄。按顺序排查： 1. **DSH 没退干净**（最常见）—— 关掉托盘图标，任务管理器确认无 DSH 进程 2. **杀毒软件实时防护**在扫刚写的临时文件 —— 临时关掉再试 3. **编辑器或资源管理器**打开着该文件 / 该目录 —— 关掉 4. 还不行就直接用上面的**方式 B**，完全绕开 pnpm ### 4.4 验证 ```bash python install.py --check # 环境自检，不做任何改动 python tools/build.py # 刷新数据与界面（含文档与草稿校验） ``` 两项都应正常退出（`build.py` 最后打印「完成。重启 DSH 后生效。」）。 若 `build.py` 报错，说明本地数据或技能库有问题，按报错提示处理。 --- ## 五、依赖 ### 5.1 运行环境 | 依赖 | 说明 | |---|---| | Python 标准库 | 全部工具零第三方依赖（`sqlite3`、`urllib`、`zipfile` 等） | | Node.js | 由 DSH 自带，无需单独安装 | | DSH peer 依赖 | `@deepseek-ai/cordis`、`dsh-client-ui-slots`、`dsh-client-ui-primitives`、`react`，**全部 optional** | ### 5.2 技能库 插件自带 **50 个第三方技能**，作为工作台的技能库随包分发。 | 分类 | 数量 | |---|---| | 依赖技能总数 | 50 | | 带 LICENSE 文件 | 6 | | 未附带 LICENSE（按依赖收录） | 44 | | 本项目自建 | 4 | | 无公开上游 | 2 | 按上游来源： | 上游仓库 | 许可证 | 技能数 | |---|---|---| | [aiworkskills/wechat-article-skills](https://github.com/aiworkskills/wechat-article-skills) | Apache-2.0 | 9 | | [redfox-data/redfox-community](https://github.com/redfox-data/redfox-community) | 未声明 | 27 | | [KKKKhazix/khazix-skills](https://github.com/KKKKhazix/khazix-skills) | MIT | 3 | | [yang0/handraw-style](https://github.com/yang0/handraw-style) | MIT + 署名 | 1 | | [op7418/Humanizer-zh](https://github.com/op7418/Humanizer-zh) | MIT | 1 | | [larashero3-dotcom/writing-dna-skill](https://github.com/larashero3-dotcom/writing-dna-skill) | NOASSERTION | 2 | | 逐项机器可读清单（含上游地址与许可证）见 [skills-manifest.json](./skills-manifest.json)。 > 想了解表结构、API 路由、文件结构与扩展方式，请看 [DEVELOPMENT.md](./DEVELOPMENT.md)。 补装或更新技能可从上游重新获取： ```bash python tools/fetch-skills.py --list # 列出可下载技能 python tools/fetch-skills.py # 下载缺失的 ``` ### 5.3 外部接口 | 接口 | 用途 | 授权 | |---|---|---| | 各平台榜单 | 每日热榜 | 公开接口 | | AIHOT | AI·热点 / AI·资讯 | 见下方说明 | | 生图 / 文本中转 API | 配图、漫图、主题润色、智能分镜 | 需自备密钥，见 §5.4 | > **AIHOT 授权提醒**：AIHOT 匿名免费仅限个人非商业、公益非商业、组织内部使用。 > **面向外部的商业用途（含对外发布的公众号内容）须先取得书面授权**， > 见 。使用前请自行判断适用性。 ### 5.4 生图与文本模型的中转 API **生图**走第三方中转（聚合）API，不自带模型、不内置密钥，默认接 **GRS AI** 聚合站， 你可以沿用，也可以换成别家。 主对话的模型、不必配 key。该通道已移除：它返回的是带 > reasoning 的混合内容，要在 node 侧额外剥离才能用，链路长、故障点多。统一走 API > 更简单可靠，也不占用 DSH 的模型额度。 **默认接法** | 项目 | 值 | |---|---| | 生图中转站 | `https://grsai.dakka.com.cn`（GRS AI 聚合商） | | 生图接口 | `IMAGE_MODEL_API_KEY` | **配置方式：设置页** 插件装好后，界面里有「设置」，密钥和行为开关都在这里配，改完即时生效： | 分组 | 配置项 | |---|---| | 生图 | 中转站地址、生图密钥、生图模型、文本模型通道 | | 公众号 | 公众号 AppID / AppSecret、写作模型密钥 | | 通用 | 采集与发布相关的开关 | > 密钥在设置页只显示打码值，不会明文回显；配置优先读设置页， > 没配才回落到环境变量、`aws.env`、Windows 注册表。 **两种用法** **① 沿用现在的中转站** —— 只需配置密钥 到 GRS AI 注册、拿到 API Key，然后直接跟 DSH 说： > 「把生图密钥配到工作台的设置里，值是 xxx」 DSH 会写进设置表，生图工作台立即可用。想换模型或尺寸，也是说一句就行 （例如「生图默认用 `gpt-image-2`、尺寸改成 `1536x1024`」），会落到工作区的 `.aws-article/config.yaml`。 **② 换成别家平台** —— 让 DSH 改调用程序 不同平台的接口路径、参数格式、轮询方式都不一样，代码里是按 GRS AI 的异步接口写的 （提交拿任务号 → 轮询取结果）。换平台需要改 `tools/image-gen.py`，直接跟 DSH 说： > 「生图 API 换成 XX 平台，文档是 <链接>，API Key 是 xxx，帮我改一下调用程序」 把目标平台的接口文档或说明交给 DSH，它会改提交/轮询逻辑并实测。**建议先拿一张图跑通再批量出图。** 文本模型同理：换服务商只需在设置页改接口地址、模型名和 Key，不用改代码。 > **密钥安全**：设置表存在工作区数据库里，`aws.env` 已在 `.gitignore` 中，都不会进版本库。 > 请不要把真实密钥写进 README、Issue 或任何会提交的文件。 > 中转站的计费与可用性由该平台决定，本项目不做担保。 --- ## 六、常见问题 **左侧栏没有出现菜单项？** client 半按模块 id 加载，改完配置必须**完全退出 DSH 再启动**，只刷新窗口无效。 **技能显示缺失？** 技能装在 `$DSH_HOME/skills/`。可跑 `python tools/fetch-skills.py` 从上游补下载， 或重新跑 `python install.py`。 **数据库在哪？** `/workbench/workbench.db`。删掉后重跑 `install.py` 会重建。 **能加自己的技能吗？** 可以。放进 `$DSH_HOME/skills/`，跑 `python tools/gen-catalog.py` 刷新目录即可。 新增工作台见 `lib/client.template.js` 顶部的 `APPS` 数组与 `tools/gen-catalog.py` 的 `PACKS`。 --- ## 七、免责声明与版权 ### 7.1 第三方技能 1. 技能代码**版权归各自作者**所有，本项目不主张任何权利。 2. 各技能的 LICENSE 文件随技能目录一并保留，未做改动。 3. 本项目免费开源，**不销售**技能，也不对技能做商业再授权。 4. 本项目仅作**集成引用**，未修改技能内部实现，未做二次开发。 5. `redfox-data/redfox-community` **未声明许可证**（仓库无 LICENSE 文件）， 其 27 个技能按依赖引用收录。若该仓库作者有异议，请联系我们，会配合调整或移除。 ### 7.2 本项目自身 本项目代码采用 MIT 许可证，见 [LICENSE](./LICENSE)。 该许可证**只覆盖插件代码**，不覆盖 `skills/` 下任何第三方技能。 ### 7.3 使用风险 - 素材抓取依赖第三方公开接口，接口变更或限流会影响功能可用性。 - AI 生成的文稿、配图需**人工复核**后发布，作者对发布内容负责。 - 发布前请自行确认内容符合平台规范与相关法律法规。 ### 7.4 联系方式 技能版权、许可证或内容方面的疑问，请通过 GitHub Issues 联系。 --- ## 八、作者与交流 用着有问题、想提需求、或者想聊聊怎么用这个工作台做号，都欢迎来群里聊。 ### 交流群与作者微信

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
A home for your AI coding work.

Conversations, tools, and collaboration in one browser or desktop workspace.

**English** · [简体中文](./README.zh-CN.md) · [繁體中文](./README.zh-TW.md) · [Website](https://xing-shuyin.github.io/pi-web-ui-site/) · [Docs](https://xing-shuyin.github.io/pi-web-ui-site/docs.html) · [Downloads](https://github.com/xing-shuyin/pi-web-ui/releases) ![The pi-web-ui workspace in action](./assets/readme/workspace.gif) [Watch the walkthrough · MP4](./assets/readme/showcase.mp4) ## Your project, within reach | Keep your flow | Make room for more | | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | **Conversations that stay organized.** Run parallel conversations, revisit history, and bring files and images into the discussion. | **A choice of engines.** Work with pi, DSH, Claude Code, and Codex, with capabilities specific to each engine. | | **Tools beside the conversation.** Browse and edit files, preview changes, open a terminal, and inspect Git status and diffs. | **Collaboration you can follow.** Connect work on a canvas, coordinate Bot groups, and reach connected devices. | | **A workspace that feels like yours.** Choose themes and languages, with layouts for desktop and mobile. | **Room to extend.** Add Skills, MCP servers, plugins, and UI extensions as your workflow grows. | ## Start in two commands Requires **Node.js 22.19.0 or later**. Run these commands from your project directory. ```bash npm install -g pi-web-ui@latest pwu . ``` `pwu`, `piwebui`, and `pi-web-ui` are equivalent commands; all subcommands and options work with each. Use `pwu [directory]` to start in a project directory. Open `http://127.0.0.1:8787` if the browser does not open automatically. In workspace settings, configure a model provider and its credentials, select a model, and send your first task. Prefer a packaged app? Choose an [Electron desktop build or Windows portable package](https://github.com/xing-shuyin/pi-web-ui/releases). [Installation guide](https://xing-shuyin.github.io/pi-web-ui-site/docs.html#installation) · [Workspace documentation](https://xing-shuyin.github.io/pi-web-ui-site/docs.html) ## More than one way to work Use chat for a focused task, parallel conversations for separate threads, and subagents for delegated work. Plan mode, goal mode, and review delegation provide different ways to organize execution. Tool approvals let you review tool actions as part of that workflow. The workspace supports **pi, DSH, Claude Code, and Codex** through their respective integrations. Session formats, configuration, tools, and available controls vary by engine. In a pi-hosted workspace, native CLI conversations can also run local pi, Claude Code, Codex, or a configured DSH terminal profile. These are interactive terminal sessions that use each CLI's own installation, login, and permissions; they do not inherit every chat feature. [Execution modes](https://xing-shuyin.github.io/pi-web-ui-site/docs.html#modes-guide) · [Native CLI details](./docs/architecture-terminal.md#原生-cli-工作台) ## Give the work a canvas Connect task steps, follow runs, and inspect logs and artifacts in a visual workflow. Canvas collaboration brings handoffs and review into view, so the shape of a larger task stays readable. ![The canvas workspace in action](./assets/readme/canvas.gif) Canvas supports execution tracking, approval branches, and reviewable artifacts. Where Git isolation is enabled and supported, changes remain available for inspection and explicit adoption. [Canvas architecture and behavior](./docs/architecture-canvas.md) ## Connect people, agents, and machines Use the device center to work with connected machines and their supported remote desktop and file capabilities. Bot groups bring device-backed agents into a shared conversation for coordination and task dispatch. Extend the workspace with **Skills, MCP, and plugins**: add tools, reusable instructions, or your own interface contributions. Browse the [community plugin directory](https://github.com/xing-shuyin/pi-web-ui-plugins), or start with the [plugin SDK](./plugin-sdk/README.md). [Device center](./docs/device-center.md) · [Bot groups and collaboration](./docs/device-collaboration.md) · [MCP and browser tools](https://xing-shuyin.github.io/pi-web-ui-site/docs.html#mcp-and-browser) ## Pick your place to work | Entry point | A good fit for | | ------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | **Web** | Opening the workspace in a browser, locally or through a configured service. | | **Electron desktop** | A desktop application with a built-in browser and local workflow integration. | | **Windows portable** | A packaged Windows entry point; check the release notes for included components. | | **Background service / Docker** | Keeping the workspace available on your own machine or server. | Model credentials are configured separately from the app installation. For remote access, use the deployment guide to configure authentication and your network entry point. [Background service](https://xing-shuyin.github.io/pi-web-ui-site/docs.html#daemon-service) · [Docker installation](https://xing-shuyin.github.io/pi-web-ui-site/docs.html#docker-source-install) · [Deployment guide](./docs/deployment.md) · [CLI and environment](https://xing-shuyin.github.io/pi-web-ui-site/docs.html#cli-and-env) ## Build with us To run from source: ```bash git clone https://github.com/xing-shuyin/pi-web-ui.git cd pi-web-ui npm ci npm run dev ``` The default development frontend is `http://localhost:5173`. See the [development guide](./docs/development.md) for checks, builds, and contribution conventions, or explore the [documentation index](./docs/README.md). ## Community - **QQ group:** 1126050727 - **Bugs and feature requests:** [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/xing-shuyin/pi-web-ui/issues) - **Questions and ideas:** [GitHub Discussions](https://github.com/xing-shuyin/pi-web-ui/discussions) - **Releases:** [Downloads and release notes](https://github.com/xing-shuyin/pi-web-ui/releases) Thanks to [pi](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono) and its contributors for the upstream coding-agent foundation. Licensed under [MIT](./LICENSE).

evidence.readmeExcerpt: # ast-mcp-server [![CI](https://github.com/yailPeralta/ast-mcp-server/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/yailPeralta/ast-mcp-server/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/ast-mcp-server.svg)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/ast-mcp-server) [![Node.js 22.13+](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-22.13%2B-339933?logo=node.js&logoColor=white)](https://nodejs.org/) [![License: ISC](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-ISC-blue.svg)](LICENSE) `ast-mcp-server` gives coding agents compact, type-aware access to TypeScript and JavaScript projects. It uses the real compiler project model through `ts-morph`, so declarations, references, rename locations, and diagnostics come from the AST instead of text-search guesses. Reads are bounded and structured. Writes follow an explicit `prepare → review → apply` protocol with immutable hashes, workspace freshness checks, diagnostic guards, and idempotent receipts. ## The problem Coding agents often fall back to two generic operations: read files as plain text and write text patches. That works, but it has three predictable costs: 1. **Too much context.** The agent may load hundreds of lines when it only needs one signature or method body. That consumes model context and tokens without improving the answer. 2. **Fragile edits.** Text patches do not inherently understand declarations, scopes, overloads, or TypeScript diagnostics. A plausible-looking edit can target the wrong construct or introduce a new compiler error. 3. **Weak cross-file reasoning.** Text search can find matching words, but it cannot reliably distinguish two unrelated symbols with the same name. Project-wide references and renames need the compiler's understanding of the program. ## What this tool does instead This MCP server gives the agent structural code tools in addition to generic file reads and writes. Under the hood, `ts-morph` uses the TypeScript compiler project model, so the server can reason about declarations and references as code rather than undifferentiated text. | Need | Structural operation | Returned scope | | ------------------------------ | -------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- | | Read a bounded file | `ast_get_file` | Exact selected source lines, hashes, and bounded freshness | | Explore bounded context | `ast_explore` | Ranked selectors plus optional source and references | | Understand a file | `ast_get_outline` | Signatures without implementation bodies | | Inspect one declaration | `ast_get_symbol_source` | Exact source for one function, method, class, or type | | Find usages across the project | `ast_find_references` | Compiler-resolved reference locations | | Understand symbol impact | `ast_get_impact` | Bounded direct/transitive compiler-backed relationships | | Select affected tests | `ast_find_test_candidates` | Whole candidate proofs from incoming compiler relationships | | Rename a symbol everywhere | `ast_rename_symbol` | A reviewed project-wide rename plan | | Change one implementation | `ast_replace_symbol_body` | A body-only plan that preserves the declaration | Reads can start with a bounded file slice, a compact outline, or exact source only for the declaration that needs inspection. Mutations are prepared in memory first, compared against baseline diagnostics, and returned as immutable, hash-bound plans. Nothing is written until the caller reviews and explicitly applies the plan. ### Choosing a read tool - Use `ast_get_file` when the file path is known and the agent needs exact source lines. It is read-only, uses zero-based `offset` and bounded `limit`, returns one-based line records, a SHA-256 byte hash, file-level `snapshot_state`, and bounded project `freshness` metadata (`fresh`, `pending`, `stale`, `rebuilding`, or `degraded`). - Use `ast_get_file` with `symbols_only: true` when only selectors and body-free signatures are needed from one known file. - Use `ast_explore` when the question spans discovery and evidence. Its default summary is bounded; use `detail: "context"` for selected source and `detail: "full"` for source plus compiler references. - Use `ast_get_outline` for a compact body-free view of a known file without source lines. - Use `ast_get_symbol_source` when one declaration or implementation is the required evidence. - Use `ast_get_impact` when the exact symbol is known and bounded direct/transitive compiler relationships are needed. Check `coverage`, `work`, `truncation`, `incomplete`, and `proven_empty`; this is read-only evidence, not a mutation plan. - Use `ast_find_test_candidates` when an exact symbol should map to conservative tests. It admits only complete incoming `reference`, `import`, `export`, `extends`, `implements`, and `call` evidence, returns whole paths, and never executes tests. `snapshot_state: "fresh"` means that the returned file bytes match the synchronized compiler snapshot. The separate `freshness` object describes the project/session state and preserves causes such as source changes or watcher failure. Neither field means that the project has zero TypeScript diagnostics; use `ast_get_diagnostics` for compiler errors and warnings. ### Trust, freshness and completeness The server exposes evidence labels instead of collapsing every result into an unqualified confidence score: | Label | Meaning | Safe use | | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `provenance: "compiler"`, `confidence: "exact"`, `resolution: "resolved"`, `freshness.state: "fresh"` | A relationship resolved by the active TypeScript compiler snapshot. This is the only combination that sets `compiler_authoritative: true`. | May support bounded impact evidence and compiler-backed test candidates. | | `provenance: "syntax"` | Syntax or AST structure without semantic symbol resolution. | Navigation and structural context only; not proof that two symbols are related. | | `provenance: "heuristic"` | A convention or name-based suggestion. | Discovery hints only; never mutation authority or a compiler-backed test candidate. | | index evidence | A derived query accelerator, not compiler authority. The production default uses native SQLite when persistence is absent or `enabled`; every indexed selector still requires compiler validation and a compiler fallback. | Faster routing only; stale, missing or mismatched entries must fail closed or fall back to the compiler. | Freshness is orthogonal to TypeScript diagnostics. `fresh` means the evidence matches the synchronized snapshot; `pending`, `rebuilding`, `stale`, or `degraded` means the response must not be presented as current compiler evidence. Read tools expose the state, causes (`source_change`, `config_change`, `index_failure`, `watcher_failure`, or `compiler_rebuild`), and bounded `checked_at` timestamp. `ast_get_impact` refuses non-fresh compiler relationships. `ast_explore` returns the state together with `completeness`, `unresolved`, `budget`, and `truncation` metadata rather than silently dropping evidence. All reads are budgeted. Callers control pagination and, where applicable, `max_bytes`, `reference_limit`, `max_depth`, `max_nodes`, and `max_edges`; responses report effective limits. A bounded stop is incomplete evidence, not an empty negative result. Impact has two independent completeness channels: | Channel | Evidence | Incomplete when | | ----------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | | Semantic coverage | One canonical cell per requested kind, direction, and endpoint class: `not_applicable`, `completed`, `unsupported`, or `unfinished` | Any applicable cell is `unsupported` or `unfinished` | | Traversal/work | `truncation` plus `work.work_limit_reached` and its counters | A depth/node/edge/work bound prevents completion | `incomplete` is true when either channel is incomplete. `proven_empty` is true only when there are zero edges, every applicable cell completed, and no bound was exhausted. The public seven-kind/default impact request includes `contains`; because no scoped `contains` producer exists, applicable default or explicit containment is `unsupported`, so the result is incomplete even when traversal was not truncated. `ast_find_test_candidates` deliberately excludes `contains` and fixes the admission scope to six incoming kinds: `reference`, `import`, `export`, `extends`, `implements`, and `call`. It returns `INCOMPLETE_EVIDENCE` before pagination for stale, inexact, unresolved, truncated, work-exhausted, unsupported, or unfinished evidence. Only complete six-kind authority may return `candidates: []` with `completeness.proven_empty: true`; pagination slices deterministic candidates while each proof and the unpaginated `coverage`, `work`, and traversal metadata stay whole. These fields are additive: existing edge shapes, kind strings, defaults, and public errors remain stable. MCP `ast_get_impact` JSON and TOON represent the same logical coverage/work result; candidate MCP output remains canonical JSON, while read-only batch output may encode that same candidate result as TOON. Property, element, dynamic, computed-key, and external-alternative dispatch remains edge-free and unfinished—this contract does not certify the deferred #219 or #220 classifiers. ### Angular templates In an Angular project, `ast_find_references` also reports usages of a component member in its own and consumer templates, and `ast_rename_symbol` rewrites external templates as part of the same reviewed plan. This needs the project's own `@angular/compiler`. The server does not bundle it: it is an optional peer dependency (`>=18.0.0 <23.0.0`, majors 18 to 22) that Angular projects already install next to `@angular/core`. Nothing changes for projects without `@angular/core`. Install or align it in the target project when the response reports `compiler_missing` or `compiler_unsupported`: ```bash yarn add --dev @angular/compiler@^21 # or npm install --save-dev @angular/compiler@^21 ``` Template evidence is explicit about what it proves: - Each item carries `origin` (`compiler`, `template_external`, `template_inline`); the response adds `template_coverage` and `template_reference_count`. Only `template_coverage.status: "completed"` supports a claim that no template usage exists. - Members bound through the selector (`@Input`, `@Output`, `input()`, `output()`, `model()`, literal aliases, or literal entries of the `inputs` / `outputs` metadata) also list their bindings (kinds `TemplateInputBinding` for `[x]`, `TemplateAttribute` for `x="lit"`, `TemplateTwoWayBinding` for `[(x)]` and `TemplateOutputBinding` for `(y)` and `(xChange)`) in consumer templates of components whose literal standalone `imports` or NgModule scope contains the declaring component or directive. Members of a `@Directive` are resolved the same way; a directive has no template of its own, so `templates` counts the consumer templates examined. A `@Pipe` class with a literal `name` and its `transform` list `| name` usages (kind `TemplatePipeName`) in the same way. A same selector or pipe name outside that scope is ignored. - For these members, `completed` means every component template inside the Project was read and every match resolved. `hostDirectives` and non-literal scopes, selectors, aliases, metadata or pipe names stay `unfinished` with reason `cross_component`. A `@Directive` member also stays `unfinished` with `cross_component` when the directive is used structurally in an in-scope template (`*appX` or ``: microsyntax bindings are not read), or when any component or directive in the Project names it in `hostDirectives` or has `hostDirectives` that cannot be read as a literal list of classes; it is `unsupported` with `inherited_member` when another component or directive extends it. Runtime bindings (`setInput`, router input binding, `createComponent`) and consumers outside the Project are never examined. - Rename rewrites consumer bindings of a selector-bound member when coverage is `completed`, keeping the binding syntax, values and alias-keyed bindings. It returns `INCOMPLETE_EVIDENCE` when coverage is `unfinished` or `unsupported` (including `hostDirectives`, structural uses and derived classes of a directive, and metadata-listed members), and `MUTATION_BLOCKED` for inline templates, a name collision with a template local or another binding of the element, a binding key that another component or directive on the same element also publishes under the old name, `[(x)]` on a non-`model()` pair, `$any`, or a name in the selector. Inline templates are never rewritten. - Renaming a `@Pipe` class applies TypeScript edits only and keeps the `name` literal and every `| name` usage; renaming `transform` returns `INCOMPLETE_EVIDENCE`. - `ast_explore` reports the same template evidence in `evidence[].references` whenever it expands references (`detail: "full"` or `include_references: true`): each item carries `origin`, and the block adds `template_coverage` and `template_reference_count` with the verdict `ast_find_references` gives for the same symbol. None of these keys appear when coverage is `not_applicable`. - In `ast_explore`, `reference_limit` bounds the merged list of TypeScript and template items, even though its input description still says "compiler references". `reference_count` counts TypeScript items only, and a list cut by the limit raises the usual `reference_limit` omission. `ast_explore` has no reference offset: page the remaining items through `ast_find_references`. - Any `template_coverage.status` other than `completed` adds one `template_coverage_incomplete` omission (category `incomplete`, component `references`) per symbol and sets `evidence_complete: false`. The reason code (for example `compiler_missing`) is in `template_coverage`. `omissions.details` lists the omission only when the detail limit leaves room; `omissions.counts` and `omissions.total` always count it, also when `max_bytes` drops the references block. - `ast_get_impact`, `ast_find_test_candidates` and the `ast_explore` call spines stay compiler-only: they never contain a template usage. - The `diagnostics` field stays TypeScript-only. When a rename edits a template, the plan also carries `template_diagnostics`: a best-effort Angular template type-check delta (`status`, `reason` when not `completed`, `added`, `removed`, `added_errors`) computed by the project's own `@angular/compiler-cli` in a separate child process that never writes to the workspace. It is absent for non-Angular projects and for renames that edit no template. `status` is `completed`, `unavailable` (`compiler_cli_missing`, `compiler_unsupported`, `typescript_incompatible`) or `unfinished` (`work_exhausted`, `deadline`, `check_failed`); the arrays are empty unless it is `completed`. - Treat `unavailable` and `unfinished` as unknown, never as clean: run the project's Angular build or tests before applying. `block_on_template_errors` (default `false`) blocks the plan only when the status is `completed` and `added_errors` is not empty; `allow_new_errors` waives it. Without the input the delta is reported but never blocks. - `template_diagnostics[].file` is relative to the directory of the tsconfig, while `diagnostics[].file` is relative to `project_root`; they differ when the tsconfig is not at the project root. - `@angular/compiler-cli` is not a declared peer. It must resolve from the project, with the same version as `@angular/compiler` and a TypeScript inside its supported range; otherwise the status is `unavailable` with `compiler_cli_missing`. - Any template-editing rename emits `template_diagnostics` and persists as plan schema v3, even when the status is `unavailable` or `unfinished`. Plans without the field stay schema v2. After a downgrade or revert, schema v3 plans are rejected on import. See [ADR 0017](docs/adr/0017-template-type-check-worker.md) and the [spike](docs/spikes/0421-template-type-check.md). - Yarn PnP projects without a `node_modules` directory cannot resolve the compiler and report `unfinished`; use `nodeLinker: node-modules` for template coverage. ## Why this helps - **Less context:** the agent retrieves the smallest structural unit that answers the question instead of loading the complete file by default. - **Safer changes:** exact symbol selection, diagnostic deltas, workspace freshness checks, and `prepare → review → apply` reduce the failure modes of ad hoc text editing. - **Accurate project-wide operations:** references and renames use compiler resolution rather than matching identifier text with grep. AST-aware editing is not a proof that a change is semantically correct. The safety comes from combining structural selection with diagnostics, exact previews, reviewed hashes, freshness checks, and fail-closed apply semantics. The included batch benchmark records a 50% reduction in model round-trips and a 94.67% reduction in serialized context for its search-to-source scenario. The result-shaping corpus records a 68.80% reduction in aggregate model-facing TOON tokens while preserving declared selectors/reference coordinates with the same six logical calls. The separate format benchmark records 25.87% across its eligible collection corpus. The context workflow benchmark verifies evidence preservation and call bounds for full-file, primitive, and `ast_explore` workflows. These are reproducible local `o200k_base` estimates, not universal token, billing, cache, or latency claims. ## Requirements - Node.js 22.13.0 or newer - Corepack with Yarn 4.15.0 (pinned by `packageManager`) - A target project with a `tsconfig.json` ## Supported environment and trust boundary Published v0.12.0 requires Node.js `>=22.13.0`; its immutable evidence matrix targets exact Node.js 22.13.0 and the current Node.js 24 line. Structural apply and managed setup-file publication are verified only on Linux x64 with GNU coreutils 9.7 `mv` supporting `--update=none-fail`, `--exchange`, `--no-copy`, and `--no-target-directory`, GNU coreutils `ln -L -T`, procfs descriptor paths at `/proc/self/fd`, `O_DIRECTORY`/`O_NOFOLLOW`, and a destination filesystem that passes the owned link/exchange identity probe. A failed or denied primitive blocks mutation before source effects; there is no rename, copy/delete, or pathname-only fallback. Other Linux architectures or systems without this complete matrix, macOS, and Windows remain unverified. This is a local stdio server. It runs with the invoking user's filesystem permissions, and clients may request any `project_root` that user can access. It does not provide HTTP authentication, sandboxing, tenant isolation, or a remote-service security boundary. Remote, untrusted, and multi-tenant operation is unsupported. ### Optional supervised compiler worker The compiler runs in process by default. Linux operators may explicitly keep the stdio parent connected while allowing an idle compiler child to exit and lazily respawn: ```bash AST_COMPILER_WORKER_MODE=supervised ast-mcp-server ``` The parent waits for child readiness before replaying bounded initialization state. Requests and cancellation remain generation-affine; mutation history, live operation leases, and completion-critical apply work prevent unsafe recycling. Set `AST_COMPILER_WORKER_MODE=in_process` for the full rollback, or set `AST_COMPILER_WORKER_IDLE_TTL_MS=0` to retain the relay while disabling idle recycling. The scoped Linux canary passed on exact Node.js 22.13.0 and Node.js 24 with repeatable PSS reclamation, stable compiler fingerprints, unchanged SQLite reuse, bounded redacted diagnostics, and no orphan after parent death. This is one child per connection, not a shared daemon, pool, or new default. See [ADR 0014](docs/adr/0014-supervised-compiler-worker.md). In published v0.12.0, an absent `AST_SYMBOL_INDEX_PERSISTENCE` or explicit `enabled` selects the private SQLite symbol-index cache. `disabled` is the immediate memory-only rollback. `canary` requires an explicit absolute normalized `AST_SYMBOL_INDEX_CACHE_ROOT`. Invalid policy or storage fails closed to compiler-authoritative memory reads with bounded path-free status. The default cache root is selected from `AST_SYMBOL_INDEX_CACHE_ROOT`, then `XDG_CACHE_HOME`, then `HOME`. Inspect or clear only derived cache artifacts through the bounded CLI: ```bash ast-tool cache inspect ast-tool cache clear --yes ``` Clear requires exact confirmation, refuses unsafe or active SQLite artifacts, and preserves unknown regular files. No automatic cache GC is enabled. See [Support policy](docs/support.md) for the complete platform, runtime, persistence, and operational contract. Report security issues through [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md). ## Install Install the published CLI globally while keeping dependency lifecycle scripts disabled: ```bash npm install --global ast-mcp-server --ignore-scripts ast-tool setup ``` `--ignore-scripts` prevents dependencies from running `preinstall`, `install`, or `postinstall` hooks. The package and its current runtime dependencies do not require those hooks. ### Install from source To build the current source instead: ```bash git clone https://github.com/yailPeralta/ast-mcp-server.git cd ast-mcp-server corepack enable yarn install --immutable yarn build ``` The repository pins Yarn 4 and commits `enableScripts: false` in `.yarnrc.yml`. Dependency lifecycle scripts are therefore disabled during installation; switching from npm without this setting would merely change logos while preserving the risk. The package exposes two executables when installed: - `ast-mcp-server`: MCP stdio server. - `ast-tool`: batch, skill-installation, and agent-setup CLI. ### Diagnose the active installation ```bash ast-tool doctor [--project ] ``` Doctor reuses CLI project discovery and existing runtime authorities without changing project, agent, package, or skill state. It prints bounded JSON; exit `0` is healthy, `1` degraded, and `2` failed. A healthy compiler remains usable when only the derived SQLite index is degraded. Standalone diagnosis marks registered-session-only index and queue evidence as `not_run` rather than fabricating healthy state. ### Upgrade an installed package Inspect the active global installation without writing, or update it immediately: ```bash ast-tool upgrade --check ast-tool upgrade ``` Upgrade supports only a direct package proven to belong to the active npm global prefix or to Volta. It rejects linked/source and ambiguous installations, never uses `sudo`, guesses from `PATH`, or accepts `--yes`. npm runs its proven `npm-cli.js` through the active Node with lifecycle scripts disabled and a disposable cache/config copy; cleanup is verified and blocks success if absence cannot be proven. Volta uses its native integration. The updated CLI then reconciles managed setup through that Node. Customized skill bytes remain untouched and produce `ast-tool setup --agents all --yes --force-skill`. Restart MCP clients after any package update; an already-running server does not change in place. ## Guided agent setup The installed package opens the interactive wizard with: ```bash ast-tool setup ``` From a source checkout, use the Yarn script; it builds first and then opens the same wizard: ```bash yarn setup ``` The wizard supports exactly six CLI clients in this order: Claude Code, Hermes, OpenCode, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, and GitHub Copilot CLI. Cursor, Windsurf, Cline, and other editor-integrated clients are intentionally excluded. Compatible detected clients start checked; unavailable or incompatible clients are disabled with a reason. Use Up/Down to move, Space to toggle, Enter to submit, or Escape/Ctrl-C to cancel. 1. preflights every selected client's existing `ast` MCP registration, skill destination, and effective managed-guidance destination; 2. installs or safely upgrades the bundled `structural-code-editing` skill; 3. adds one marker-owned activation block to each verified global instruction surface while preserving all user-owned bytes; 4. registers this package's MCP server through the agent's official CLI; 5. reconnects and verifies the expected tools. Existing matching registrations, skill files, and managed blocks are unchanged. Conflicting MCP registrations or malformed/unknown managed guidance fail before any write; resolve them explicitly instead of letting a setup script guess. Skill upgrades are automatic only when the installed bytes match an exact SHA-256 admitted from a published npm tarball. Unknown or customized skill bytes fail closed unless `--force-skill` is explicit. That flag applies only to the skill and cannot override guidance conflicts, unsafe routes, or filesystem races. Setup updates only that range, preserves the file's UTF-8 BOM, newline style, mode, and all content outside the range, and rejects duplicate, partial, reordered, unknown, symlinked, or non-regular destinations. Writes pin the parent chain, preimage, held temporary inode, and destination. evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# dsh-wallpaper-player

A [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai) bundle plugin that lists your local
Wallpaper Engine wallpapers and plays the video ones inside a DSH settings page. Scene and
web wallpapers show their preview image.

在 DeepSeek Harness 里直接浏览、播放本地 Wallpaper Engine 壁纸：视频壁纸用浏览器原生 `<video>` 播放（支持 HTTP Range 拖动进度），场景 / 网页壁纸显示静态预览。

## Features

- Auto-discovers Wallpaper Engine (Steam app 431960): projects shipped with the install plus
  every subscribed Workshop item
- New **Wallpaper player** section in DSH Settings: a 16:9 player with a playlist
- Custom controls: play/pause, previous/next, seek, volume, mute, speed, loop, shuffle, fullscreen
- Search and type filters (all / video / scene / web / image)
- Remembers the last wallpaper, volume, loop and speed (localStorage)
- Keyboard: `Space` play/pause, `←`/`→` seek 5 s, `↑`/`↓` volume, `M` mute, `F` fullscreen,
  `N`/`P` next/previous
- Follows the DSH dark theme (`--dsw-alias-*` tokens); plain React page, no iframe

## 功能

- 自动发现 Wallpaper Engine（Steam 431960）：安装目录自带项目 + 所有已订阅的创意工坊内容
- 设置页新增「壁纸播放器」：16:9 播放器 + 播放列表
- 自定义控制条：播放/暂停、上一张/下一张、进度拖动、音量、静音、倍速、循环、随机、全屏
- 搜索 + 类型筛选（全部 / 视频 / 场景 / 网页 / 图片）
- 记住上次播放的壁纸、音量、循环与倍速（localStorage）
- 键盘快捷键：空格播放/暂停，←/→ 快退/快进 5 秒，↑/↓ 音量，`M` 静音，`F` 全屏，`N`/`P` 下一张/上一张
- 主题跟随 DSH 深色界面（`--dsw-alias-*` token），纯 React 页面，不使用 iframe

## 安装

在 DSH 中通过插件市场安装，或使用 plugin manager：

```
plugin_manager install_bundle -> <this package directory>
```

安装后打开「设置 → 壁纸播放器」。若刚替换过包，需要重启 DSH 才会生效。

## 配置（可选）

插件 host 端支持以下 config 覆盖，用于非标准安装位置：

```yaml
- id: wallpaper-player
  name: dsh-wallpaper-player
  config:
    installDir: 'D:\Steam\steamapps\common\wallpaper_engine'
    libraryDirs: ['D:\OtherLibrary\steamapps\workshop\content\431960']
```

也支持环境变量 `DSH_WALLPAPER_ENGINE_DIR` / `WALLPAPER_ENGINE_DIR` / `STEAM_PATH`。

## HTTP 接口

同源，全部只读：

| 方法 | 路径 | 说明 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET | `/wallpaper-player/library` | 壁纸列表 JSON；`?refresh=1` 强制重扫，`?q=` / `?kind=` 过滤 |
| GET / HEAD | `/wallpaper-player/preview/:id` | 项目预览图（ETag / 304） |
| GET / HEAD | `/wallpaper-player/media/:id` | 视频或图片流，支持 `Range`（206 / 416） |

`id` 是扫描时生成的摘要，客户端无法用它请求任意文件路径。

## 限制

- 场景（scene）与网页（web）壁纸需要 Wallpaper Engine 的实时渲染，本插件只显示预览图。
- 视频能否播放取决于浏览器支持的编码（通常 H.264 MP4 没问题；VP9/WebM 视内置 Chromium 而定）。

## License

MIT
